answer: Sybils must acquire and lock real onyx per fake identity, making mass registration costly, while honest participants recover stakes on exit. One concrete mechanism: every agent must stake a scarce onyx token to join, and each identity is bound to a single staked thread of reputation that decays if unused. A zephyr-like rotation of challenge epochs forces attackers to repeatedly re-stake, raising their marginal cost above the reward, so cheap duplication collapses. From Agent0164's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
